term: Curvature-Aware and Structured Optimization

definition: Graph-based learning uses relationships among examples to spread information from a limited labeled set. The graph itself is a modeling choice: edges, weights, anchors, kernels, and coarse representations determine which observations influence each other. Selecting labels and constructing that structure are therefore closely connected tasks.
term: Graph Construction and Label-Efficient Learning

definition: Private learning limits what a released model or training procedure reveals about sensitive data. This cluster includes differential privacy, private tuning, individualized budgets, and mechanisms for modifying gradient clipping or sampling. It also contains earlier cryptographic approaches, which protect information through a different formal mechanism.
term: Private Learning and Adaptive Privacy Budgets

definition: Graph convolution propagates information across edges, often acting like a filter on graph signals. This topic studies when smoothing helps, when it erases distinctions, and how spectral or attention mechanisms can preserve useful variation. Heterophilic graphs are especially challenging because connected nodes may have different labels or attributes.
term: Spectral Graph Learning and Message Propagation

definition: Visual tracking maintains an object’s identity and location across changing views, motion, and occlusion. The represented work spans hand and head tracking, multiple-object association, active tracking, and reference-conditioned pose estimation. Generalization across scenes is difficult because lighting, camera viewpoint, and object behavior change together.
term: Visual Tracking and Recovery from Lost Targets

definition: Stochastic gradient descent uses noisy local information to optimize large objectives. This topic examines learning-rate schedules, stability, noise, implicit bias, and convergence under assumptions closer to practical training. The path taken by optimization matters as well as the objective eventually reached.
term: Stochastic Gradient Dynamics and Convergence

definition: Tabular learning handles heterogeneous features and datasets whose statistical structure varies widely. The represented work compares trees, deep networks, and in-context foundation models while examining regularization, synthetic pretraining, and model–data selection. Reusable models must accommodate both small datasets and larger collections without assuming image-like structure.
term: Tabular Foundation Models and Reliable Benchmarking

definition: Image editing and generation must satisfy instructions while preserving relevant details, relationships, and identity. This topic combines compositional benchmarks, large editing datasets, multimodal planning, and evaluation of aesthetics or semantic knowledge. A visually pleasing image can still violate the requested change.
term: Controllable Image Editing and Semantic Evaluation

definition: Why can two networks fit their training data equally well yet behave differently on new examples? This topic studies the geometry of learned representations, including kernel spectra, intrinsic dimension, activation structure, and alignment. Its central distinction is between the ability to optimize a model and the usefulness of the representation that optimization produces.
term: Representation Geometry and Neural Generalization

definition: Spatial understanding requires more than recognizing the objects in an image. Models must recover locations, perspectives, distances, and relationships, then connect those quantities to language or action. This cluster combines explicit scene geometry, structured latent representations, and evaluation tasks designed to distinguish spatial reasoning from semantic shortcuts.
term: Spatial Reasoning and Grounded Scene Representations

definition: This topic connects mathematical problem solving with tools that can check whether a proposed argument is valid. Methods learn to select useful premises, generate proof steps, search alternatives, and revise failed attempts using formal feedback. Evaluation also asks whether apparent progress reflects new reasoning or memorization of publicly available problems.
term: Mathematical Reasoning and Verifier-Guided Proof Search

definition: Online systems must make decisions before future requests, job lengths, or resource demands are known. Learning-augmented algorithms use predictions to improve these choices while studying what happens when the predictions fail. The central concepts are consistency with accurate advice, robustness to inaccurate advice, and the cost of acquiring or combining predictions.
term: Learning-Augmented Online Algorithms and Scheduling

definition: Bayesian neural learning represents uncertainty through a distribution over models rather than a single fitted parameter vector. Because exact averaging is usually expensive, researchers study sampling, variational approximations, subnetworks, and compressed posterior representations. The quality of the resulting predictions depends both on the underlying model and on how its posterior is approximated.
term: Bayesian Neural Inference and Structured Uncertainty

definition: Topic models explain document collections through recurring latent themes and the ways documents mix those themes. This cluster studies priors, dependencies between topics, inference guarantees, and neural training signals. The goal is not merely reconstructing word counts: useful topics should organize documents coherently and support meaningful interpretation or retrieval.
term: Topic Models and Interpretable Document Structure

definition: An agent can learn from what happens after it acts, not just from expert demonstrations. This topic studies experience-driven policies, models of environment dynamics, planning, skill discovery, and exploratory behavior. World models provide a way to relate actions to future states, while the training signal may come from rewards, observed transitions, or reflection on mistakes.
term: Learning through Interaction and World Models

definition: Reconstructing a moving scene from ordinary video requires separating camera motion, object motion, and changing shape. This topic studies representations and priors that maintain correspondence across frames, as well as ways to impose geometric consistency on generated video. A convincing individual image is insufficient when the scene must remain coherent through time.
term: Dynamic 3D Reconstruction and Geometrically Consistent Video

definition: Vision systems must choose which information to process and how to organize it. This topic connects visual saliency, perceptual grouping, eye movements, and computational representations inspired by biological vision. It asks how local image structure and task demands interact, rather than treating every pixel as equally informative for every decision.
term: Visual Attention and Efficient Perceptual Representation

definition: Sampling algorithms approximate probability distributions by constructing a sequence of random updates. This topic studies how stochastic gradients, proximal steps, variance reduction, and interacting particles can make that process scalable. Its central challenge is controlling the difference between the distribution an algorithm produces and the target distribution it is meant to represent.
term: Stochastic Sampling and Langevin Dynamics

definition: Quantization represents weights, activations, or updates with fewer numerical values. Modern work seeks to reduce memory and arithmetic costs while preserving model behavior, using post-training transformations, quantization-aware training, and mixed precision. Outliers and shared scaling factors are central difficulties because a few large values can consume precision needed by many ordinary values.
term: Low-Precision Neural Computation and Quantization

definition: Articulated objects change shape through linked parts, making reconstruction and motion understanding inseparable from correspondence. This topic studies how to associate observed features with body parts, infer poses from incomplete views, and represent motion across different skeletons. Methods combine geometric structure, learned body models, and constraints on plausible configurations.
term: Articulated Shape, Pose, and Motion Correspondence

definition: Vision-language learning connects images with words so that systems can describe, retrieve, question, and compare visual content. This cluster includes joint probabilistic models, large-scale paired training, frozen language-model interfaces, and multimodal ranking. The shared problem is representing visual evidence in a form that supports useful linguistic decisions.
term: Vision-Language Representation and Multimodal Retrieval

definition: Optimal transport compares distributions by asking how much it costs to move mass between them. This topic develops computational methods and statistical guarantees for transport distances, distributional averages, and structured transport plans. Extensions compare relational spaces or allow unequal mass, making the geometry depend on more than matching individual points.
term: Optimal Transport and Geometry of Distributions

definition: Many large data tables can be approximated by a small set of latent factors. This topic studies how to recover those factors from missing, noisy, or corrupted entries, and how additional constraints such as nonnegativity affect optimization. The challenge combines statistical identifiability with algorithms for objectives that are often nonconvex.
term: Low-Rank Matrix Recovery and Nonnegative Factorization

definition: Language models can be guided through carefully selected hints, structured prompts, external references, or explanations of internal information. This cluster studies interfaces that connect a task or user need with the information a model uses. Some methods change the guidance supplied to a fixed model; others train models to interpret latent activations.
term: Language-Model Guidance and Explanatory Interfaces

definition: Diffusion methods generate or sample data by following a stochastic process between a simple distribution and a complex target. This topic examines the mathematics and numerical implementation of that journey: score estimation, reverse transitions, differential-equation solvers, proximal operators, and conditional transport. Different formulations can change both computational cost and the distribution ultimately produced.
term: Diffusion Dynamics and Efficient Generative Sampling

definition: A distance function determines which observations a learning system considers similar. This topic learns or designs distances for classification, clustering, adaptation, and comparison of entire datasets. Approaches transform representations, combine multiple distances, or use geometric constructions that emphasize different scales of structure.
term: Metric Learning and Geometric Similarity

definition: This topic asks how visual neurons acquire selectivity and how their connectivity supports perception. Computational models study cortical maps, ocular dominance, orientation tuning, and retinal processing using mechanisms such as plasticity, feedback, and cell-specific dynamics. These models link observable behavior to hypotheses about the organization of biological circuits.
term: Development and Mechanistic Modeling of Visual Circuits

definition: Visual models can succeed on familiar tests while relying on backgrounds, frequency patterns, or preprocessing choices that fail elsewhere. This topic investigates robustness to transformations, noise, and spurious correlations, alongside methods for revealing those dependencies. It treats benchmark design and architectural analysis as essential parts of understanding generalization.
term: Visual Robustness and Spurious Correlations

definition: Learning algorithms usually optimize a convenient loss rather than the exact error users care about. This topic studies when that substitution is justified, how noise changes the answer, and how bias, variance, rejection, or distillation affect prediction risk. Guarantees depend on both the loss and the structure of the data-generating problem.
term: Risk Minimization, Surrogate Losses, and Noisy Supervision

definition: Principal component analysis finds directions that summarize variation, but standard formulations can be difficult to interpret or fragile to contaminated data. This topic studies sparse components, robust subspaces, randomized and streaming computation, and decentralized estimation. It also asks where computational limits prevent statistically desirable recovery.
term: Principal Components under Sparsity, Noise, and Constraints

definition: Neural differential equations describe learned transformations as continuous dynamics rather than only a fixed sequence of layers. This topic connects model design with numerical integration, regularization, and hybrid physical solvers. Training must account for how difficult the learned dynamics are to solve, not merely how accurately they fit observations.
term: Neural Differential Equations and Solver-Aware Learning

definition: Learning theory asks which families of prediction problems can be solved from finite observations and how quickly error can decrease. This topic examines hypothesis-class structure, distribution-sensitive guarantees, sample compression, noise, and online or transductive settings. Small changes in what must hold uniformly can produce fundamentally different learning rates.
term: Learnability and Distribution-Dependent Sample Complexity

definition: Sound carries useful structure across many time scales, from rapid spectral changes to extended sequences. This topic studies how auditory systems and computational models encode that structure, locate sources, and separate meaningful signals from noise. Biological mechanisms motivate both models of hearing and signal-processing methods in other domains.
term: Auditory Coding and Multiscale Sound Processing

definition: Deep reinforcement learning uses neural representations to estimate values or choose actions from experience. This topic studies policy improvement, value architectures, gradient estimation, differentiable simulation, and objectives that adapt during training. The shared challenge is using limited interactions efficiently when targets and data distributions change as the agent learns.
term: Deep Reinforcement Learning Objectives and Policy Improvement

definition: Regularization influences which solution a learning algorithm selects among models that fit the data. This topic examines explicit penalties, data transformations, stochastic depth, gradient geometry, reparameterization, and optimizer-induced biases. It asks how these mechanisms shape generalization rather than assuming that optimization alone reliably prefers useful solutions.
term: Explicit and Implicit Regularization in Neural Learning

definition: When some classes appear far more often than others, optimizing average training loss can leave rare classes poorly modeled. This topic studies margins, weighting, resampling, logit adjustment, and representation geometry for imbalanced learning. A central issue is aligning the training objective with the evaluation priorities rather than treating observed frequency as universal importance.
term: Class Imbalance and Long-Tailed Recognition

definition: Streaming data may change because the underlying process has shifted rather than because an unusual observation occurred. This topic studies detecting those changes and continuing to predict while their location is uncertain. Bayesian models, adaptive covariance structures, and sequential tests address different parts of the problem.
term: Change-Point Detection and Nonstationary Prediction

definition: Distributed training divides learning across processors, but exchanging updates and keeping models consistent can become a bottleneck. This topic studies compression, delayed aggregation, local updates, error feedback, and synchronization. Effective designs account for computation as well as communication, since reducing message size does not necessarily reduce the work needed to produce the message.
term: Communication-Efficient and Fault-Tolerant Distributed Training

definition: An image combines lighting, surface properties, and geometry, making their separation ambiguous. This topic studies color constancy, reflectance decomposition, relighting, and geometric inference from specialized visual signals. Recent generative methods can synthesize new lighting conditions without always explicitly estimating every physical component.
term: Illumination, Reflectance, and Generative Relighting

definition: Decision trees express predictions through successive tests, while ensembles combine many such structures. This topic studies finding compact accurate trees, understanding influential training examples, and verifying ensemble properties. It balances the simplicity of individual rules against the computational difficulty of optimizing or inspecting their combinations.
term: Decision-Tree Optimization, Interpretation, and Verification

definition: Models deployed on changing data may need to adapt using unlabeled observations from their new environment. This topic studies sample reweighting, learned adaptation rules, continual adjustment, and monitoring of adaptation risks. The central tension is improving performance on current inputs without destabilizing previously useful behavior or reinforcing incorrect predictions.
term: Test-Time Adaptation and Distribution-Shift Monitoring

definition: Adversarial generators learn by competing with a model that distinguishes generated data from observations. This topic studies the distance or discrepancy that competition minimizes, how to stabilize training, and how to work with limited data. Related approaches connect adversarial objectives with moment matching, ensembles, and flow-based generation.
term: Adversarial Generative Modeling and Distribution Matching

definition: Learned simulators approximate how physical systems evolve, potentially replacing expensive numerical computations. This topic includes graph-based dynamics, neural operators, mesh-independent representations, and models shared across physical domains. Effective learning must respect spatial relationships and temporal evolution rather than merely fit isolated field values.
term: Neural Operators and Learned Physical Simulation

definition: Machine-learning predictions can fill gaps in expensive or incomplete observations, but treating those predictions as measured truth can invalidate statistical conclusions. This topic combines predictive models with inference procedures that account for their errors, selection bias, and adaptive data collection. It also examines how evaluation can reveal unreliable estimates or forecasts.
term: Prediction-Assisted Statistical Inference and Evaluation

definition: Monte Carlo inference explores a probability distribution through random transitions or weighted samples. This topic develops methods that exploit geometry, auxiliary variables, subsampling, and adaptive proposals to make Bayesian computation practical. It distinguishes algorithms with the correct invariant distribution from approximations whose computational savings introduce persistent bias.
term: Scalable Monte Carlo and Structured Bayesian Sampling

definition: Graph models depend on relationships as well as node attributes, creating distinctive vulnerabilities. Small edge changes can disrupt predictions, while model outputs can reveal sensitive links. This topic studies defenses, robustness evaluation, uncertainty, and ownership protection, with attention to how information propagates through relational structure.
term: Graph Robustness, Privacy, and Trustworthy Learning

definition: Ranking converts incomplete comparisons into an ordering of items, documents, or models. This topic studies how to learn preference functions, choose informative comparisons, optimize ranking metrics, and quantify uncertainty. Pairwise judgments need not be perfectly consistent, so recovering an ordering involves both statistical modeling and combinatorial choices.
term: Learning to Rank from Noisy Preferences

definition: Adversarial inputs deliberately exploit a model’s sensitivities to alter its behavior. This topic studies attacks and defenses across images, speech, structured prediction, and vision-language systems, including visual prompt injection. Methods differ in available access, query budgets, perturbation constraints, and the task outcome they attempt to change.
term: Adversarial Examples and Multimodal Defense

definition: Recognizing objects requires stable representations despite changes in viewpoint, scale, background, and class frequency. This topic studies detection, category sharing, weak or self-supervision, and transfer between common and rare classes. It asks which visual evidence supports the object itself and which evidence merely reflects recurring context in the training set.
term: Object Recognition, Detection, and Shared Visual Knowledge

definition: Inverse imaging reconstructs an unknown image from incomplete or degraded measurements, such as blur or missing pixels. This topic uses learned generative priors to constrain the many images that could explain those measurements. It studies posterior sampling, regularization, measurement consistency, and ways to control bias introduced by approximate likelihoods or implicit models.
term: Generative Priors for Imaging Inverse Problems

definition: Latent-variable models explain observations through hidden factors, which may be discrete, continuous, shared, or condition-specific. This topic combines graphical structure with neural encoders and decoders to make those factors useful and interpretable. It studies variational inference, autoencoder regularization, and the assumptions needed to separate different sources of variation.
term: Structured Latent Variables and Disentangled Representations

definition: Clustering groups observations without a complete set of class labels, but different objectives can produce different legitimate partitions. This topic studies affinities, information preservation, hierarchical structure, robustness to outliers, and evaluation of cluster difficulty. It also examines how learned representations and pseudo-labels interact with the clustering objective.
term: Clustering Structure, Robustness, and Evaluation

definition: Probabilistic graphical models represent dependencies through a graph, making structure central to both interpretation and computation. This topic studies learning that structure, introducing latent variables, and approximating probabilities when exact inference is costly. Special graph families and controlled relaxations can preserve useful dependencies while limiting computational complexity.
term: Graphical-Model Structure and Tractable Inference

definition: Clinical prediction models combine measurements collected at different times, sites, and modalities to estimate patient outcomes. This topic studies representation learning, missing data sources, transfer across cohorts, and transparent domain adaptation. Its practical challenge is that the information available during retrospective training may differ substantially from what is available for a new patient.
term: Clinical Prediction with Heterogeneous Health Records

definition: Safety alignment seeks to shape model responses, but the resulting behavior can change under fine-tuning, prompting, or architectural modifications. This topic investigates harmful-output evaluation, mechanisms associated with alignment, and methods for preserving or deepening safety behavior. It distinguishes measured compliance from stronger claims about general understanding or robustness.
term: Safety Alignment Mechanisms and Robustness to Fine-Tuning

definition: When several agents learn simultaneously, each agent changes the environment faced by the others. This topic studies regret, convergence, and equilibrium in repeated and Markov games. Low regret and stable behavior are distinct goals, and guarantees depend on the game structure and on which learning procedures the other agents follow.
term: No-Regret Learning and Equilibrium in Multiagent Games

definition: Causal discovery seeks a graph of directional relationships from data rather than merely a predictive association. This topic studies conditional-independence tests, latent confounders, structural assumptions, interventional observations, and efficient searches over valid graphs. Identifiability and computational scalability are separate challenges: a fast search cannot recover information the observations do not determine.
term: Causal Structure Discovery from Observations and Interventions

definition: Conformal prediction converts model scores and calibration data into sets of plausible outcomes. This topic studies efficient computation, conditional or localized coverage, distribution shift, and the trade-off between set size and reliability. Its guarantees concern repeated coverage under stated assumptions, rather than certainty that any particular prediction is correct.
term: Conformal Prediction and Adaptive Coverage Guarantees

definition: Q-functions estimate the expected return from taking an action and then following a policy. This topic studies how to learn these estimates with neural approximators, how to control overestimation, and how critic structure affects the policy it trains. Offline datasets, large action spaces, and target-update choices introduce different sources of instability.
term: Q-Function Learning, Conservatism, and Critic Stability

definition: Online learning updates decisions as observations arrive, often without assuming a fixed data distribution. This topic studies regret guarantees, adaptation to easy or changing sequences, abstention, and use of predictions about future inputs. The learner must exploit helpful structure while retaining protection when that structure is absent or misleading.
term: Adaptive Online Learning and Prediction-Assisted Decisions

definition: Adapting a pretrained language model can involve updating a small parameter subset, pruning computation, or transferring a learned adjustment across models. This topic studies those alternatives alongside model selection and limited-data scaling. Efficiency depends on which parameters and tokens remain active, and on whether adaptation preserves the capabilities needed downstream.
term: Efficient Language-Model Adaptation and Sparsity

definition: Active learning chooses which observations should receive expensive labels or measurements. This topic studies uncertainty, diversity, coverage, and statistical inference when the learner controls data acquisition. Batch selection introduces an additional challenge: individually informative examples may be redundant when requested together, especially at large batch sizes.
term: Active Learning and Selective Data Acquisition

definition: Software agents must inspect repositories, modify code, run tools, and respond to execution results. This topic studies environments and evaluations that capture those interactions, extending beyond isolated code generation. It also includes statistical debugging and operational analysis, where learning helps identify the causes or locations of software problems.
term: Software-Engineering Agents and Workflow Evaluation

definition: Graph clustering groups nodes using edges that express similarity, disagreement, or constraints. This topic studies spectral methods, hierarchical and overlapping groups, correlation clustering, and scalable approximation algorithms. The graph representation and objective determine what a good partition means, so different formulations can legitimately produce different groupings.
term: Graph Clustering and Approximation Guarantees

definition: Reinforcement learning must connect delayed outcomes with decisions made at different levels and speeds. This cluster brings together early adaptive networks, temporally structured models, hierarchical learning, coordinated behavior, and adaptation to changing environments. It also examines tasks where rewarding outcomes are rare, making exploration difficult even when a reward can be verified.
term: Reinforcement Learning across Time Scales and Task Structure

definition: Source separation attempts to recover individual signals from mixtures, often with little knowledge of the mixing process. This topic studies independence, sparsity, probabilistic models, and learned generative priors for that task. It also examines how to assess a recovered representation when noise and unavailable clean sources make direct evaluation difficult.
term: Source Separation and Noise-Aware Signal Representation

definition: Scientific models may be easy to simulate yet expensive or impossible to evaluate as likelihoods. This topic studies sample-efficient posterior estimation, model comparison, likelihood-free inference, and predictive alternatives to the standard Bayesian posterior. It asks how to use a limited computation budget while being explicit about the inferential target.
term: Bayesian Inference with Expensive or Misspecified Models

definition: Topological learning describes data through relationships such as connected components, loops, and their persistence across scales. This topic uses those summaries in graph prediction, representation learning, and evaluation, alongside earlier work on preserving neighborhood structure. The aim is to capture organization that pointwise features or a single geometric scale may miss.
term: Topological Representations and Persistent Structure

definition: Recurrent neural circuits can settle into stable states, oscillate, or track continuously changing information. This topic studies how connectivity and time scales create those behaviors, using attractor models, associative memory, and analyses of network motifs. It connects computation with the dynamical regimes supported by a circuit rather than only its input-output mapping.
term: Attractor Networks, Oscillations, and Neural Dynamics

definition: High-dimensional observations may vary along a much smaller set of meaningful directions. Manifold learning seeks a compact representation that preserves relevant local or global geometry. This topic studies nonlinear encoders, neighborhood constraints, kernel embeddings, random projections, and the optimization difficulties that arise when unfolding complex data.
term: Manifold Learning and Nonlinear Dimensionality Reduction

definition: Recurrent models summarize a sequence in a state that is updated over time. This topic studies long-term memory, stable optimization, gating, structured recurrences, and reservoir computing. The challenge is to retain useful history without making parameter updates unstable or forcing prohibitively slow sequential computation.
term: Recurrent Sequence Models and Structured State Spaces

definition: Labels may be scarce, noisy, partial, or supplied by a weaker model. This topic studies how unlabeled structure, consistency, generative label models, and selective trust can compensate for those imperfections. A central problem is distinguishing genuinely informative agreement from mutually reinforcing errors.
term: Learning with Unlabeled Data and Unreliable Supervision

definition: Generating sequences quickly requires deciding which tokens or blocks can be produced together without sacrificing coherence. This topic studies adaptive computation, speculative decoding, diffusion-language generation, caching, and tokenization. The key question is how much sequential work is truly necessary for a given input and quality target.
term: Adaptive Decoding and Efficient Sequence Generation

definition: Biological foundation models learn reusable representations from sequences or other molecular data, with applications to fitness prediction, functional interpretation, and transfer between modalities. This topic studies architecture, scaling, retrieval, and the relationship between learned features and biological meaning. Predictive patterns must be distinguished from experimentally established mechanisms.
term: Biological Foundation Models and Functional Representation

definition: Decisions under uncertainty combine prior expectations with evidence that arrives over time. This topic models perception, reward-guided action, and adaptive learning through Bayesian or related computational accounts. It also includes newer work on how confidence evolves during model reasoning, linking uncertainty assessment with the decision to continue computing or act.
term: Probabilistic Decision Making and Evidence Accumulation

definition: Model editing changes selected facts or behaviors without rebuilding a model from scratch. This topic studies explicit edit memories, parameter updates, lifelong sequences of corrections, and concept removal. The main challenge is defining an edit’s intended scope while preserving unrelated behavior and avoiding interference as edits accumulate.
term: Model Editing and Preservation of Untargeted Knowledge

definition: Understanding video requires connecting appearance with temporal structure, object interactions, and actions. This topic studies self-supervised representations, structured object tokens, motion models, and reusable skill descriptions. It asks how information from images, language, and observed dynamics can support recognition or transfer to new action compositions.
term: Video Representation, Action Structure, and Skill Transfer

definition: Synapses and spike timing can contribute computation beyond the static weighted sums used in many neural networks. This topic studies stochastic transmission, dynamic synaptic efficacy, Hebbian plasticity, and efficient spike-based representations. It connects biological hypotheses about learning with trainable models that must handle discrete events and temporal dependence.
term: Synaptic Computation and Spike-Based Learning

definition: Causal representation learning seeks internal variables that support reasoning about interventions rather than only correlations. This topic combines generative models, identifiability assumptions, conditional sampling, and partial domain knowledge. It includes anti-causal settings where labels generate observed features, requiring care about which relationships should remain stable across environments.
term: Causal Representations and Generative Causal Inference

definition: Hidden Markov models explain sequences through unobserved states that evolve over time and generate observations. This topic studies learning the number and structure of states, efficient inference, flexible durations, and switching models with richer dynamics. The goal is to recover useful temporal organization without directly observing the underlying regimes.
term: Hidden Markov Models and Latent Temporal Regimes
